name: hfs
description: Rank one item across Hype, Facts and Signal

hype.instructions: How much of the item in `title` and `excerpt` (the page text) is hype: largely baseless, overhyped, overrated, not driven by true value, exaggerated, heavy opinion or investment bias, or far more popular than its substance? Use `section_keywords.hype` and the reader's `taste_examples` as hints.

facts.instructions: How checkable are the claims in `excerpt` and `findings`, judged from what the text itself shows? A primary source (the maker's own announcement, release notes, a changelog, documentation, code, a paper) or specific, checkable details (versions, numbers, dates, named sources) score high. Claims with no source score low. Score the evidence the text shows, not whether you checked it yourself. Use `section_keywords.facts` as hints.
criteria: Primary source or specific, checkable details
Primary source with code, numbers or a release

signal.instructions: How useful, valuable and specifically actionable is the item in `title` and `excerpt` for an engineer who builds with AI agents, right now? Use `section_keywords.signal` as hints.
